## Principle

The test/train split and the cross-validation folds are **one problem**, not
two. Pili et al. (2025) report internal CV with no stated holdout; CAST
(`geodist`/`knndm`) gives a prediction-matched holdout *or* a fold diagnostic,
but not a single object that derives both from the same logic. Here the
partition is one artifact whose:

- **unit** is the *connected component* (a graph of nearby points), not an
  arbitrary `k`;
- **separation** is measured on **two explicit axes** — geography (governs
  leakage / connectivity) and environment (governs representativeness /
  coverage) — kept separate because the cases where they *decouple* are exactly
  the ecologically interesting ones;
- **split and fold rules** are parameterized by `purpose ∈ {discovery, mapping,
  projection}`, because "can this cluster be split?" is not a property of the
  cluster — it is a property of the question being asked.

The failure this is built to avoid: on bimodal / clustered rare-plant data,
both E-clustering (collapse a cluster to one point) and vanilla LOPO/NNDM (hold
a whole cluster out) destroy the within-condition replication that a sparse
endemic needs. We want clusters that can be **cut and re-represented** when the
question is *mapping*, and held out intact when the question is *discovery*.

We build this piecewise: every step emits its intermediate object **and** a
plot, so we can see the graphs before anything is folded into a function. The
per-step helpers (`partition_*`) compose into the final `build_partition()` at
the end.

## Parameters

Everything tunable lives here so the rest of the document is logic, not knobs.

```{r params}
params_part <- list(
  resolution     = 90,            # nominal res for the env stack (90/30/10/3 -> dem_3arc/1arc/1-3arc/3m)
  connect_m      = 250,           # Step 1 graph edge threshold (metres). Derived/justified in Step 1.
  superclust_m   = 40000,         # Step 2a super-cluster cut (metres), inside the 30-75 km gap
  train_target   = c(0.70, 0.80), # Step 4 outer test-holdout: soft train-proportion window
  n_folds        = 10,            # Step 5 inner CV folds (each validates ~1/n_folds of training)
  purpose        = "mapping",     # discovery | mapping | projection
  pca_var_target = 0.90,          # retain enough env PCA axes to reach this cumulative variance
  min_split_n    = 12,            # Step 3: min presences for a component to be worth cutting
  mode_sep_factor = 1.5,          # Step 3: env_nn / ref mode-radius above this = a resolved env mode
                                  #   (higher ⇒ fewer forced-train singletons ⇒ more small env-isolated
                                  #    units allowed into test as flagged extrapolation points)
  seed           = 1021
)
set.seed(params_part$seed)
```

## Setup

This document runs from the **repository root** (set via `knitr$opts_knit$root.dir`
in the YAML), so every path below is root-relative. Source the project's
`functions.R` for `rastReader()`, `res_string()`, `assign_population()`, etc.
`PROJ_ROOT` defined in that file is the data-machine path; the raster probe below
also checks a local `data/spatial/processed` and prefers whichever actually holds
the stack.

```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(terra)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(igraph)
})

source("scripts/functions.R")  # defines PROJ_ROOT (data-machine), rastReader, res_string, ...

p2dat   <- "data/Data4modelling"
p2areas <- "data/GroundTruthPts/ground_truth_median-VISITED.gpkg"
# raster stack may live under the data-machine root or locally; Step 0 probes both
p2proc_candidates <- c(
  file.path(PROJ_ROOT, "data", "spatial", "processed"),
  "data/spatial/processed"
)
```

## Step 0 — Points, populations, and the environmental space

The **presences are the graph unit** — the population structure we want to see —
so they drive Steps 1–2. We load the collated iter2 set
(`3m-presence-iter2.gpkg`), which folds the **2026 field records** (opportunistic
+ transect) into the iter1 presences; `source` carries provenance so the 2026
points are visible on every plot. Background **absences** (`iter1-pa.gpkg`, the
2026 campaign added presences, not new background) are loaded aside here and
only enter in the class-aware Steps 4–5. Then we extract predictors and reduce
to a PCA env space; if the raster stack isn't mounted, Steps 1–2 still run on
geography alone.

```{r step0-points}
# presences: iter2 collated set (iter1 + 2026 field data). Occurrence = 1.
# keep point_id to join the pre-extracted predictor CSV in step0-env.
pts <- st_read(file.path(p2dat, "3m-presence-iter2.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  transmute(Occurrence = 1L, point_id = as.character(point_id),
            source = as.character(source), site = as.character(site),
            .id = row_number())

# background absences, held aside for the class-aware split/folds (Steps 4–5).
bg <- st_read(file.path(p2dat, "iter1-pa.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  transmute(Occurrence = 0L, source = "iter1-pa", site = NA_character_)

cat(nrow(pts), "presences (",
    paste(sprintf("%s: %d", names(table(pts$source)), table(pts$source)), collapse = ", "),
    ") +", nrow(bg), "background absences\n")
```

```{r step0-env}
# Attach environmental predictors + PCA scores. Prefer the pre-extracted CSV
# (point_id join — no rasters needed on this machine); fall back to on-the-fly
# raster extraction if the stack is mounted; else Steps 1–2 run on geography alone.
pred_csv <- file.path(p2dat, "3m-presence-iter2-10m-predictors.csv")
res_str  <- res_string(params_part$resolution)
p2proc   <- p2proc_candidates[file.exists(file.path(p2proc_candidates, paste0("dem_", res_str)))][1]
coord_cols <- c("point_id", "source", "date", "site", "X", "Y", "Longitude", "Latitude")

env <- NULL
if (file.exists(pred_csv)) {
  preds <- readr::read_csv(pred_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(point_id = as.character(point_id))
  env_vars <- setdiff(names(preds)[vapply(preds, is.numeric, logical(1))], coord_cols)
  env <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(point_id) |>
    left_join(select(preds, point_id, all_of(env_vars)), by = "point_id") |>
    select(all_of(env_vars))
  message("Predictors from CSV (", length(env_vars), " vars, point_id join).")
} else if (!is.na(p2proc)) {
  rast_dat <- rastReader(paste0("dem_", res_str), p2proc)
  env <- terra::extract(rast_dat, pts, ID = FALSE)
  env <- env[, vapply(env, is.numeric, logical(1)), drop = FALSE]
  message("Predictors from raster stack at ", p2proc, " (", ncol(env), " vars).")
}

env_ok <- !is.null(env)
if (env_ok) {
  cc     <- complete.cases(env)
  pca    <- prcomp(env[cc, ], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
  # retain enough axes to reach the cumulative-variance target (data-driven, not fixed)
  cumvar <- summary(pca)$importance[3, ]
  n_pca  <- as.integer(which(cumvar >= params_part$pca_var_target)[1])
  scores <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(env), n_pca,
                   dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("PC", seq_len(n_pca))))
  scores[cc, ] <- predict(pca, env[cc, ])[, seq_len(n_pca)]
  pts <- bind_cols(pts, as_tibble(scores))
  cat(sprintf("PCA env space: %d axes for %.0f%% variance (%.1f%% achieved); %d presences missing predictors.\n",
              n_pca, 100 * params_part$pca_var_target, 100 * cumvar[n_pca], sum(!cc)))
} else {
  message("No predictors available; Steps 1–2 run on geography alone.")
}
```

```{r step0-plot}
# presences coloured by provenance — the 2026 field data shown explicitly
ggplot(pts) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = source), alpha = .8, size = 1.8) +
  labs(title = "Step 0 — presences by source (2026 field data folded in)",
       colour = "source") +
  theme_minimal()

if (env_ok) {
  ggplot(pts, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = source)) +
    geom_point(alpha = .8, size = 1.8) +
    labs(title = "Step 0 — environmental (PCA) space, by source", colour = "source") +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

## Step 1 — Graph construction (connected components in geographic space)

Connect any two points within `connect_m`; the connected components of that
graph are our partition units. Graph-based (vs k-means / fixed-k) because it
respects the real gaps in irregular, bimodal data: a dense population becomes
one component we *can* later split, an isolated outlier becomes its own
singleton component we handle explicitly.

### Deriving the threshold (don't trust the round number)

`connect_m` is the master knob — it decides whether two nearby populations are
one component (held together) or two (splittable). Rather than default it, look
at the presence-to-presence nearest-neighbour distance distribution and put the
threshold at the gap between within-population and between-population scales.
(On the data machine, also compare against `CAST::geodist()`'s
sample-to-prediction distances — the knee there is the principled choice.)

```{r step1-threshold}
# pts are all presences; NN distance between each presence and its nearest other
nn_m <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(
  pts, pts[sf::st_nearest_feature(pts), ], by_element = TRUE))

tibble(nn_m = nn_m) |>
  ggplot(aes(nn_m)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = params_part$connect_m, colour = "red", linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Step 1 — presence NN-distance distribution (red = chosen connect_m)",
       x = "nearest-neighbour distance (m, log10)", y = "count") +
  theme_minimal()

quantile(nn_m, c(.5, .75, .9, .95, .99)) |> round(1)
```

### Build components

```{r step1-graph}
partition_components <- function(x, connect_m) {
  within <- sf::st_is_within_distance(x, dist = connect_m)  # sparse list, includes self
  g      <- igraph::graph_from_adj_list(within, mode = "all")
  memb   <- igraph::components(g)$membership
  x$component <- factor(memb)
  attr(x, "adj") <- within   # keep for edge plotting / hull distances
  x
}

pts <- partition_components(pts, params_part$connect_m)
cat("components:", nlevels(pts$component),
    "| sizes:", paste(sort(table(pts$component), decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(8, nlevels(pts$component))],
                      collapse = ", "), "...\n")
```

```{r step1-plot}
# edge list from the sparse within-distance object (small n, cheap)
adj   <- attr(pts, "adj")
co    <- sf::st_coordinates(pts)
edges <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(adj), function(i) {
  j <- adj[[i]][adj[[i]] > i]
  if (length(j)) cbind(x = co[i, 1], y = co[i, 2], xend = co[j, 1], yend = co[j, 2]) else NULL
})) |> as.data.frame()

ggplot() +
  { if (nrow(edges)) geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                                  colour = "grey70", linewidth = .3) } +
  geom_sf(data = pts, aes(colour = component), size = 1.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Step 1 — graph components (connect_m = %d m)", params_part$connect_m)) +
  theme_minimal()

# where does the 2026 field data land across the distance-based components?
pts |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(component, source) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(desc(rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))))
```

## Step 2 — Inter-component geographic distance (minimum, hull-cheapened)

Leakage is about the *closest* points between components, so we want the
**minimum** nearest distance, not centroid distance. Collapsing each component
to a MULTIPOINT and taking `st_distance` gives the exact pairwise minima; for
large components this is where the convex-hull shortcut goes (only hull
vertices can carry the minimum).

```{r step2-geo}
partition_geo_dist <- function(x, hull = FALSE) {
  parts <- x |>
    group_by(component) |>
    summarise(do_union = TRUE, .groups = "drop")        # one (MULTI)geometry per component
  if (hull) parts <- st_convex_hull(parts)
  d <- sf::st_distance(parts)                            # min distance between geometries
  units::drop_units(d) -> d
  dimnames(d) <- list(levels(x$component), levels(x$component))
  d
}

geo_d <- partition_geo_dist(pts)
as.data.frame(round(geo_d)) |> head(8)
```

```{r step2-plot}
as.data.frame(as.table(geo_d)) |>
  setNames(c("a", "b", "dist_m")) |>
  ggplot(aes(a, b, fill = dist_m)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "sqrt") +
  labs(title = "Step 2 — min geographic distance between components", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 6))
```

## Step 2a — Inter-component environmental distance + the geo/env decoupling diagnostic

Component location in env space = medoid of its PCA scores (robust to the
stochastic within-cluster spread). The key diagnostic — **before** building any
rule — is how the geographic and environmental between-component distances
relate. The global Spearman rho is *not* the whole story: for this species the
scatter is **two clouds and a gap** (a ~30–75 km geographic gap separating
population super-clusters), and the relationship is non-linear and strongly
heteroscedastic. The decisive feature is the **conditional env spread at small
geographic distance** — if geographically adjacent components span a wide env
range, geographic folds will *not* control environmental extrapolation and the
two axes must stay separate.

Empirically here: `rho ≈ 0.64`, but within ~25 km env distance ranges from ~0
to the maximum, and the two most spatially extreme components are env-*closer*
than mid-range pairs (far in space, near in env). Colouring the env-space
ordination by **geographic super-cluster** (a single-linkage cut across the
30–75 km gap) shows why: at the *super-cluster* scale geo and env largely agree
(Cochetopa-south and the eastern outliers are the distinct env mode), while
*within* the northern massif env varies independently of geography. That split
is exactly the `purpose` hierarchy — super-cluster = discovery unit,
within-super-cluster = mapping unit.

```{r step2a-env, eval=env_ok}
partition_env_dist <- function(x, pcs) {
  sc <- x |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(component, all_of(pcs))
  medoids <- sc |>
    group_by(component) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(pcs), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")
  m <- as.matrix(medoids[, pcs]); rownames(m) <- medoids$component
  as.matrix(dist(m))
}

pcs   <- grep("^PC", names(pts), value = TRUE)
env_d <- partition_env_dist(pts, pcs)

# align and correlate the off-diagonal pairs
ut <- upper.tri(geo_d)
decouple <- tibble(geo_m = geo_d[ut], env_d = env_d[ut])
rho <- cor(decouple$geo_m, decouple$env_d, method = "spearman")

ggplot(decouple, aes(geo_m / 1000, env_d)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .35, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "red", linewidth = .6) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Step 2a — geo vs env between-component distance (Spearman rho = %.2f)", rho),
       x = "min geographic distance (km)", y = "env (PCA medoid) distance") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Geographic super-clusters and the env-space view

A single-linkage cut of the component min-distance matrix across the 30–75 km
gap recovers the geographic super-clusters. Colouring the env-space ordination
by them is the plot that resolves the structure: where a super-cluster occupies
its own env region (geo≈env, discovery-valid holdout) versus where one
super-cluster smears across env space (geo⊥env, mapping needs env-aware folds).

```{r step2a-superclusters, eval=env_ok}
# super-clusters: single-linkage so the cut respects the inter-cluster gap, not centroids
superc <- cutree(hclust(as.dist(geo_d), method = "single"), h = params_part$superclust_m)
pts$supercluster <- factor(superc[as.character(pts$component)])
cat(length(unique(superc)), "geographic super-clusters at a ",
    params_part$superclust_m / 1000, " km cut; component counts:\n")
print(table(superc))

med <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(component, supercluster) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(pcs), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(med, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = supercluster, size = n)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .75) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = component), size = 2.3, max.overlaps = 40,
                           show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 10)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(title = "Step 2a — component medoids in env space, by geographic super-cluster",
       subtitle = "single-linkage cut at 40 km; size = n presences") +
  theme_minimal()
```


---

# Decision-bearing steps

The pieces above are the *inputs*. Steps 3–5 encode the design choices. Step 3
is now implemented; Steps 4–5 remain scaffolded (`eval: false`) with real
signatures and `TODO` decision points.

## Step 3 — Separation & splittability (purpose-dependent)

Splittability is **not** a property of a component — it is `separation × purpose`.
A component well-separated in environment is the most *dangerous* one to split
under `discovery` (splitting an env-distinct unit turns an honest extrapolation
test into near-interpolation) and the most *useful* one to split under `mapping`
(you want within-condition interpolation). Grounded in Step 2a: the **super-cluster
is the discovery atom** (geo≈env between super-clusters), while **within** a
super-cluster env ⊥ geo, so mapping needs env-aware cutting.

Separation is measured without inverting a per-component covariance (unstable for
the many tiny components): a **silhouette-like** ratio of each component's gap to
its nearest neighbour in env space (`env_nn`) over a **stable global mode-radius**
— the median internal env dispersion of the *well-populated* components
(`n ≥ min_split_n`). Using a global reference rather than each component's own
spread is essential: a 1–2 point component has near-zero spread, so its own ratio
would blow up and falsely flag it as a distinct mode. `mode_sep > mode_sep_factor`
⇒ the component is a *resolved env mode*. The gate:

- **mapping** — `splittable` if a component is large enough to cut
  (`n ≥ min_split_n`); a resolved env mode that is *too small to cut*
  (`env_isolated & n < min_split_n`, e.g. the 2026 discovery comp 37) is a
  **`singleton_mode`**: it can be neither split nor honestly held out, so it is
  forced into train and flagged (held out, it would guarantee extrapolation
  failure — that belongs to a discovery fold, not a mapping average).
- **discovery** — keep every unit intact (`splittable = FALSE`); the holdout atom
  is the super-cluster.
- **projection** — defer to env-space thinning (E-clustering / E-distThinning).

```{r step3-splittable, eval=env_ok}
partition_splittable <- function(x, geo_d, env_d, pcs, purpose,
                                 min_split_n = 12, mode_sep_factor = 1) {
  xd    <- sf::st_drop_geometry(x)
  comps <- levels(x$component)

  # medoid per component, and each component's internal env dispersion
  med <- xd |> group_by(component) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(pcs), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  P   <- as.matrix(xd[pcs])
  Pm  <- as.matrix(med[match(xd$component, med$component), pcs])
  spread <- tibble(component = xd$component, d2med = sqrt(rowSums((P - Pm)^2))) |>
    group_by(component) |> summarise(env_spread = mean(d2med), .groups = "drop")

  # stable global mode-radius: median spread of well-populated components (falls
  # back to all components if none clear min_split_n). Avoids the tiny-component
  # spread→0 degeneracy that would flag every small cluster as its own mode.
  well <- med$component[med$n >= min_split_n]
  ref_spread <- stats::median(spread$env_spread[spread$component %in% well])
  if (!is.finite(ref_spread)) ref_spread <- stats::median(spread$env_spread)

  # nearest OTHER component in each space
  gd <- geo_d; diag(gd) <- Inf
  ed <- env_d; diag(ed) <- Inf
  near <- tibble(component = comps, geo_nn = apply(gd, 1, min), env_nn = apply(ed, 1, min))

  tab <- distinct(xd, component, supercluster) |>
    left_join(select(med, component, n), by = "component") |>
    left_join(spread, by = "component") |>
    left_join(near,   by = "component") |>
    mutate(
      mode_sep     = env_nn / ref_spread,               # >factor ⇒ resolved env mode
      env_isolated = mode_sep > mode_sep_factor,
      splittable   = if (purpose == "mapping") n >= min_split_n else FALSE,
      must_train   = purpose == "mapping" & env_isolated & n < min_split_n,
      role = dplyr::case_when(
        purpose == "discovery"  ~ "atomic (supercluster = unit)",
        purpose == "projection" ~ "defer to env thinning",
        must_train              ~ "singleton_mode (force train, flag)",
        splittable              ~ "splittable",
        TRUE                    ~ "atomic (env-redundant)"))
  attr(tab, "ref_spread") <- ref_spread   # stable mode-radius, reused by Step 4
  tab
}

spl <- partition_splittable(pts, geo_d, env_d, pcs, params_part$purpose,
                            params_part$min_split_n, params_part$mode_sep_factor)
ref_spread <- attr(spl, "ref_spread")
cat("purpose =", params_part$purpose, "| ref mode-radius =", round(ref_spread, 2),
    "| role counts:\n"); print(table(spl$role))
arrange(spl, desc(n))
```

```{r step3-plot, eval=env_ok}
med_role <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(component, supercluster) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(pcs), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(spl, component, role, mode_sep), by = "component")

# env-space: which components are splittable / atomic / singleton modes
ggplot(med_role, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = role, size = n)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .8) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = component), size = 2.2, max.overlaps = 40,
                           show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 10)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Step 3 — splittability in env space (purpose = %s)", params_part$purpose),
       subtitle = "size = n presences") +
  theme_minimal()

# geography: where the roles fall
pts_role <- left_join(pts, select(spl, component, role), by = "component")
ggplot(pts_role) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = role), size = 1.4, alpha = .8) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(title = "Step 3 — component roles on the map") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Step 4 — Test/train split (two-axis, soft 70–80 %, two-sided coverage)

First pass, `purpose = "mapping"`. The Step-3 roles make the **two-sided
coverage** rule fall out automatically, so the allocation is simple:

1. **`singleton_mode` → train** (forced; held out they would guarantee
   extrapolation, which is a discovery question, not a mapping one).
2. **`splittable` → cut and re-represented**: within each such component take a
   **k-means-medoid** test subset — cluster the component in the retained env
   space into `n_test` groups and take the point nearest each centre. The medoids
   are *representative/interior* (not extremes), and every component's extremes
   stay in train, so both sets span the mode while test stays in-distribution.
3. **`atomic` → whole-unit filler, most env-isolated first**: held out intact to
   top the test set up toward the budget, prioritising the most env-isolated units
   so the extrapolation budget is spent deliberately (and flagged by the coverage
   check) rather than left to a random draw.

The train proportion is a **soft target** — test comes first from the splittable
fractions, then whole atomics are added greedily until the achieved proportion
lands in `train_target`; nothing is forced across the line point-by-point.

Coverage is **measured against the training set's own structure, not an arbitrary
radius** (the NNDM idea from the CAST vignette): compare each test point's nearest
env distance to *train* against the distribution of train→train nearest-neighbour
distances. Where the test NN distribution tracks the train NN distribution, those
test points are representative — an interpolation task. We **report** rather than
forbid the tail: the fraction of test beyond the train-NN 95th percentile and
beyond its max. With `mode_sep_factor` set loosely (so fewer small env-isolated
units are forced to train), some of those units are deliberately held into test
as **flagged harder-than-interpolation points** — material the model is scored on
even though train barely covers it. Note that *beyond-max* is typically ~0 here:
forcing the most-isolated units into train keeps the train envelope env-
comprehensive, so the realized extrapolation signal lives in the **beyond-p95
tail**, not beyond-max. That tail fraction is the extrapolation budget made
explicit; downstream it can be scored separately from the interpolation bulk. A true `geodist`-style comparison against
*sample-to-prediction* distances still needs the prediction grid and runs on the
data machine.

```{r step4-split, eval=env_ok}
partition_split <- function(x, spl, pcs, train_target, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  xd <- st_drop_geometry(x) |> left_join(select(spl, component, role), by = "component")
  N  <- nrow(xd)
  test_frac   <- 1 - mean(train_target)
  target_test <- round(N * test_frac)

  # k-means-medoid sampler: representative (not extreme) spread over all env axes
  kmed_pick <- function(M, n_pick) {
    n <- nrow(M)
    if (n_pick >= n) return(seq_len(n))
    if (n_pick < 1)  return(integer(0))
    n_pick <- min(n_pick, nrow(unique(M)))     # kmeans needs centers <= distinct points
    km <- suppressWarnings(stats::kmeans(M, centers = n_pick, nstart = 5, iter.max = 50))
    vapply(seq_len(n_pick), function(k) {
      idx <- which(km$cluster == k)
      idx[which.min(rowSums((M[idx, , drop = FALSE] -
                             matrix(km$centers[k, ], length(idx), ncol(M), byrow = TRUE))^2))]
    }, integer(1))
  }

  test_id <- integer(0)

  # 2. splittable: within-component representative test subset
  for (cmp in spl$component[spl$role == "splittable"]) {
    idx  <- xd$.id[xd$component == cmp]
    M    <- as.matrix(xd[match(idx, xd$.id), pcs])
    pick <- idx[kmed_pick(M, round(length(idx) * test_frac))]
    test_id <- c(test_id, pick)
  }

  # 3. atomic: add whole units until the budget is met, MOST env-isolated first, so
  #    the extrapolation budget is spent deliberately on the genuinely novel units
  #    (flagged by NNDM coverage below) rather than by luck of a random draw.
  atomic_order <- spl |>
    filter(role == "atomic (env-redundant)") |>
    arrange(desc(mode_sep)) |>
    pull(component)
  for (cmp in atomic_order) {
    if (length(test_id) >= target_test) break
    test_id <- c(test_id, xd$.id[xd$component == cmp])
  }

  train_id <- setdiff(xd$.id, test_id)           # singletons + the rest

  # NNDM-style coverage: test->train NN env distances vs train->train NN distances
  Ptr <- as.matrix(xd[match(train_id, xd$.id), pcs])
  Pte <- as.matrix(xd[match(test_id,  xd$.id), pcs])
  test_nn  <- apply(Pte, 1, function(p) sqrt(min(colSums((t(Ptr) - p)^2))))
  train_nn <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(Ptr)),
                     function(i) sqrt(min(colSums((t(Ptr[-i, , drop = FALSE]) - Ptr[i, ])^2))),
                     numeric(1))

  by_unit <- xd |>
    mutate(set = if_else(.id %in% test_id, "test", "train")) |>
    count(component, role, set) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    mutate(across(any_of(c("train", "test")), as.integer))

  list(
    train_id = train_id, test_id = test_id, by_unit = by_unit,
    achieved_train_prop = length(train_id) / N, target_test = target_test,
    nn = list(train = train_nn, test = test_nn),
    coverage = list(
      frac_beyond_p95 = mean(test_nn > stats::quantile(train_nn, 0.95)),
      frac_beyond_max = mean(test_nn > max(train_nn)))
  )
}

split <- partition_split(pts, spl, pcs, params_part$train_target, seed = params_part$seed)

cat(sprintf("train prop achieved: %.3f (target %.2f-%.2f); test n = %d (target ~%d)\n",
            split$achieved_train_prop, params_part$train_target[1], params_part$train_target[2],
            length(split$test_id), split$target_test))
cat(sprintf("NNDM coverage: %.1f%% of test beyond train-NN p95; %.1f%% beyond train-NN max\n",
            100 * split$coverage$frac_beyond_p95, 100 * split$coverage$frac_beyond_max))
split$by_unit
```

# geography

## Step 5 — CV folds (same logic, every unit out ≥ 1)

Folds are built over the **training set** (Step 4's `train_id`) — the inner
tuning CV nested inside the outer test holdout — and are *not* leave-one-graph-out.
`k = n_folds` (10 by default, matching `modeller`'s `knndm(..., k = 10)`), so each
fold validates ~1/k of training — independent of the outer `train_target` holdout.
The Step-3 roles drive assignment, with the same philosophy as Step 4:

- **`splittable` → spread across folds**: k-means the component's training points
  into k groups, one per fold, so each fold validates ~1/k of the component and
  trains on the rest — the component is always re-represented in training.
- **`atomic` / `singleton` → whole unit to one fold**, load-balanced so fold sizes
  stay even. Every such unit is therefore **held out in exactly one fold** —
  satisfying "every unit out ≥ 1", including the env-isolated singletons.

Per fold we record the NNDM-style **beyond-p95 tail** and how many **singleton**
(extrapolation) points it validates, so folds heavy in extrapolation content can
be scored *separately* from the interpolation bulk rather than averaged in.
Output mirrors `CAST::knndm()` (`indx_train` / `indx_test`, positional row indices
into the training frame) so `modeller()`'s `trainControl(index = ...)` consumes it
unchanged.

```{r step5-folds, eval=env_ok}
partition_folds <- function(x, spl, pcs, train_id, n_folds = 10, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  xt <- st_drop_geometry(x) |> filter(.id %in% train_id) |>
    left_join(select(spl, component, role, mode_sep), by = "component")
  xt$row <- seq_len(nrow(xt))                       # positional index into the training frame
  k <- as.integer(n_folds)
  fold <- integer(nrow(xt))

  # splittable: spread each component's training points across the k folds
  for (cmp in unique(xt$component[xt$role == "splittable"])) {
    idx <- which(xt$component == cmp)
    M   <- as.matrix(xt[idx, pcs])
    kk  <- min(k, nrow(unique(M)))            # cap at distinct env points
    cl  <- if (kk <= 1)          rep(1L, nrow(M))
           else if (kk >= nrow(M)) seq_len(nrow(M))   # each point its own cluster (avoids kmeans centers==nrow edge)
           else suppressWarnings(stats::kmeans(M, centers = kk, nstart = 5, iter.max = 50)$cluster)
    fold[idx] <- ((cl - 1) %% k) + 1
  }

  # atomic + singleton: whole unit -> one fold, greedily load-balanced
  whole <- xt |> filter(role != "splittable") |> count(component, name = "n") |> arrange(desc(n))
  load  <- tabulate(fold[fold > 0], nbins = k)
  for (cmp in whole$component) {
    f <- which.min(load); idx <- which(xt$component == cmp)
    fold[idx] <- f; load[f] <- load[f] + length(idx)
  }

  indx_test  <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) xt$row[fold == f])
  indx_train <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) xt$row[fold != f])

  fold_meta <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(k), function(f) {
    in_val <- fold == f                      # bind before tibble() (a `fold` column would shadow it)
    tr <- as.matrix(xt[!in_val, pcs]); te <- as.matrix(xt[in_val, pcs])
    tnn <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(tr)),
                  function(i) sqrt(min(colSums((t(tr[-i, , drop = FALSE]) - tr[i, ])^2))), numeric(1))
    enn <- apply(te, 1, function(p) sqrt(min(colSums((t(tr) - p)^2))))
    n_sing <- sum(grepl("singleton", xt$role[in_val]))
    tibble(fold = f, n_val = nrow(te), val_prop = nrow(te) / nrow(xt),
           beyond_p95 = mean(enn > stats::quantile(tnn, 0.95)),
           n_singleton_val = n_sing)
  })

  list(indx_train = indx_train, indx_test = indx_test, k = k,
       fold = setNames(fold, xt$.id), fold_meta = fold_meta)
}

folds <- partition_folds(pts, spl, pcs, split$train_id, params_part$n_folds,
                         seed = params_part$seed)
cat(sprintf("k = %d folds over %d training points; every unit held out >= 1.\n",
            folds$k, length(split$train_id)))
folds$fold_meta
```

ggplot(fold_pts) +

## Step 6 — Class-aware assembly (presences + absences → one caret-ready frame)

Presences carry the spatial structure, so they keep the structured partition from
Steps 4–5. **Absences do not form populations to hold out and (as real
observations, or as env-distance PAs that key off the whole presence cloud) carry
no leakage worth protecting against here**, so they get the *nice-and-easy* path: a
random outer train/test split at the same proportion, and balanced random
assignment to the 10 folds. Random still keeps ~`(k-1)/k` of absences in every
fold's training and preserves the presence:absence ratio in each set.

The output is one fixed frame tagged `set` (train/test) and `fold`, plus
`caret`-shaped `indx_train` / `indx_test` (positional into the *training* rows), so
`caret::train(trainControl(index = …, indexOut = …))` consumes it unchanged.

> **On the data machine:** the proper Option-A flow regenerates the env-distance PA
> pool *against the outer-train presences only* right after the presence split, then
> feeds that pool here. Running without rasters, we assign the existing absence pool
> (`bg`, `iter1-pa.gpkg`) instead — the assignment logic is identical (random), only
> the PA provenance differs. Absences need no env here; predictors are attached at
> fit time.

```{r step6-classes, eval=env_ok}
partition_classes <- function(pts, bg, split, folds, train_target, n_folds, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  k <- n_folds
  test_prop <- 1 - mean(train_target)

  # presences: structured assignment from Steps 4-5 (test presences get fold = NA)
  pres <- tibble(
    id    = paste0("pres_", pts$.id),
    class = 1L,
    set   = if_else(pts$.id %in% split$test_id, "test", "train"),
    fold  = unname(folds$fold[as.character(pts$.id)]))

  # absences: random outer split, then balanced random folds within the train side
  nb  <- nrow(bg)
  aid <- paste0("abs_", seq_len(nb))
  a_set <- rep("train", nb); a_set[sample.int(nb, round(nb * test_prop))] <- "test"
  a_fold <- rep(NA_integer_, nb)
  tr <- which(a_set == "train")
  a_fold[tr] <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(tr)))      # balanced across folds
  abs <- tibble(id = aid, class = 0L, set = a_set, fold = a_fold)

  combined <- bind_rows(pres, abs)
  tf <- combined[combined$set == "train", ]; tf$row <- seq_len(nrow(tf))
  indx_test  <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) tf$row[which(tf$fold == f)])
  indx_train <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) tf$row[which(tf$fold != f)])

  list(combined = combined, train_frame = tf,
       indx_train = indx_train, indx_test = indx_test,
       test_ids = combined$id[combined$set == "test"])
}

classes <- partition_classes(pts, bg, split, folds, params_part$train_target,
                             params_part$n_folds, seed = params_part$seed)

# class balance per set, and presence:absence ratio
classes$combined |>
  count(set, class) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(absence = `0`, presence = `1`) |>
  mutate(ratio_abs_per_pres = round(absence / presence, 2))
```

```{r step6-foldbalance, eval=env_ok}
# per-fold class balance in the combined training frame (what caret will tune on)
classes$train_frame |>
  filter(!is.na(fold)) |>
  count(fold, class) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(absence = `0`, presence = `1`) |>
  mutate(n_val = absence + presence, pres_frac = round(presence / n_val, 2))
```

The single artifact every downstream consumer reads. Shape deliberately
mirrors `spatial_class_split()` + `knndm()` so `modeller(split = ...)` and
`trainControl(index = ...)` both work, and it subsumes LOPO (populations =
components), edist folds (split within env-homogeneous components), and the
whole-population-leakage audit (the two-sided coverage rule) in one object.

`x` already carries the PCA env columns (Step 0) and `pcs` names them; `bg` is the
absence/background set.

```{r build-partition, eval=env_ok}
build_partition <- function(x, bg, pcs, p) {   # p = params_part
  x     <- partition_components(x, p$connect_m)
  geo_d <- partition_geo_dist(x)
  x$supercluster <- factor(
    cutree(hclust(as.dist(geo_d), method = "single"), h = p$superclust_m)[as.character(x$component)])
  env_d   <- partition_env_dist(x, pcs)
  spl     <- partition_splittable(x, geo_d, env_d, pcs, p$purpose, p$min_split_n, p$mode_sep_factor)
  split   <- partition_split(x, spl, pcs, p$train_target, p$seed)
  folds   <- partition_folds(x, spl, pcs, split$train_id, p$n_folds, p$seed)
  classes <- partition_classes(x, bg, split, folds, p$train_target, p$n_folds, p$seed)

  list(
    # presence-level structure
    train_id   = split$train_id,
    test_id    = split$test_id,
    components = select(st_drop_geometry(x), .id, component, supercluster),
    geo_d = geo_d, env_d = env_d, splittable = spl,
    split_coverage = split$coverage, fold_meta = folds$fold_meta,
    # class-aware frame for fitting (caret-ready)
    combined   = classes$combined,        # every point: id, class, set, fold
    train_frame = classes$train_frame,
    indx_train = classes$indx_train,      # positional into train_frame, for caret::trainControl(index=)
    indx_test  = classes$indx_test,       # ...and indexOut=
    test_ids   = classes$test_ids,
    meta = p[c("connect_m", "superclust_m", "train_target", "n_folds", "purpose",
               "pca_var_target", "min_split_n", "mode_sep_factor", "seed")]
  )
}

# single-call check: reproduces the inline Steps 1-6 and returns the caret-ready object
part <- build_partition(pts, bg, pcs, params_part)
ntr <- nrow(part$train_frame)
stopifnot(
  identical(sort(part$train_id), sort(split$train_id)),            # same presence split
  all(tabulate(unlist(part$indx_test),  nbins = ntr) == 1),        # each train row validated once
  all(tabulate(unlist(part$indx_train), nbins = ntr) == params_part$n_folds - 1)
)
cat(sprintf("build_partition() OK: %d train / %d test presences; %d-row class-aware frame; %d folds; %d test ids.\n",
            length(part$train_id), length(part$test_id), ntr, length(part$indx_train), length(part$test_ids)))
part$combined |> count(set, class) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(absence = `0`, presence = `1`)
```

## Open questions carried forward

- **`connect_m` derivation** — formalise the variogram-range / geodist-knee
  choice instead of the default; sensitivity-test across resolutions.
- **Separation metric** (Step 3) — Mahalanobis space, covariance estimator,
  and the "alone" radii in geo and env.
- **The objective** (Steps 4–5) — the exact W/coverage score that balances
  "test looks like prediction" against "train covers test".
- **Out-of-AOA folds** — the coverage test that routes a fold to the separate,
  discovery-style score rather than the mapping average.
```
